verdict: Palo Alto Networks grew revenue 16% to $2.47B and earned $334M — a steady, profitable start to the year, with the big CyberArk acquisition still to come.

segments.name: Subscription & support
segments.note: Security subscriptions and support — the recurring core of the business.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling security platforms to enterprises — the largest running cost.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up sharply from $98M a year ago, with acquisition activity under way.

otherDetail: Other income, net of $103M, with no interest expense in the quarter.
oneTimers: Share-based compensation was $387M, acquisition-related costs $5M, amortization of acquired intangible assets $39M and litigation-related charges $6M — together they explain most of the gap between the $334M GAAP net income and $662M of non-GAAP net income.
Palo Alto announced its intent to acquire Chronosphere in this release; the previously announced CyberArk acquisition had not yet closed, so neither deal's revenue or costs are in these numbers.
footerNote: Palo Alto guided Q2 FY26 revenue to $2.57B–$2.59B in this release.

takeaways.title: Steady growth
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 16% to $2.47B — product revenue rose 23% to $434M and subscription and support 14% to $2.04B.

takeaways.title: The platform bet is working
takeaways.text: Next-Generation Security ARR grew 29% to $5.9B, and remaining performance obligations rose 24% to $15.5B.

takeaways.title: Profitably run
takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $334M, just below $351M a year ago as G&A rose with acquisition activity — operating income still grew to $309M from $286M.
